findings.title: Escape does not close the create or edit modal when focus is on the Severity or State dropdown
findings.requirement: specs/features/06-create-bug.md Scenario: User can close the create-bug modal with the Escape key; specs/features/09-edit-bug.md Scenario: User can close the edit-bug modal with the Escape key
findings.evidence: New in this diff. After choosing a value with the dropdown (focus stays on the closed select), Escape leaves the modal open: create (Severity), edit (Severity) and edit (State) all fail toBeHidden. Screenshots: evidence/functional/test-results/diff/diff-regressions-06-Escape-*/, diff-regressions-09-Escape-*/, diff-regressions-09-13-Esc-*/. Nothing is saved, so no data is lost, but the spec says Escape anywhere in the open modal acts like Cancel. tests/accessibility/accessibility.spec.ts:62 asserts this non-spec behaviour; Playwright's press() does not open the popup, so the test proves the closed-select case.
findings.repro: Log in, New Bug, type a title, choose HIGH in Severity, press Escape: the modal stays open.
findings.fix: Drop the tagName === 'SELECT' condition from both Escape handlers (the native popup consumes its own Escape) and change the a11y test to expect the modal to close. If the team wants Escape to be ignored on a select, spec 06/09 must say so first.

findings.title: Edit modal enables Save when a field holds only a zero-width space; the server then rejects it
findings.requirement: specs/features/09-edit-bug.md Scenario: Save button is disabled when any required field is blank
findings.evidence: The backend (bugService.ts isBlank) and the create modal now treat zero-width-only values as blank, but the edit modal's hasBlank only trims. Changing title, owner or description to U+200B leaves Save enabled (diff-regressions '09 Save is disabled when ... zero-width space', 3 failures). Clicking Save: PUT 400 {"error":"blank_description"}, modal shows "Description is required.", stored value unchanged (evidence/functional/zw-save-probe.txt, zw-save-probe.png). The create modal blocks it correctly (diff-regressions '06 a zero-width-only title', pass).
findings.repro: Open a bug, replace Description with a single U+200B: Save is enabled.
findings.fix: In EditBugModal, reuse the create modal's isBlank (strip [\u200B-\u200D\u2060\uFEFF] and then trim) for hasBlank and validate()

findings.title: Search regression: removing punctuation means "log in" no longer finds "log-in" and "save load" no longer finds "save/load"
findings.requirement: specs/features/11-search-board.md Design: normalize punctuation on both sides of the match; Scenario: Typing in the search field filters bugs by title
findings.evidence: The functional-01 fix deletes punctuation, so "save/load broken" becomes "saveload broken". Query "save load broken <token>" and query "log in <token>" (for "Issue with log-in <token>") return 0 rows (diff-regressions '11 search ...', screenshots in test-results/diff/diff-regressions-11-search-*). Both matched on baseline, where punctuation became a space. The spec's example still passes; the regression is in cases the old rule handled.
findings.repro: Create "save/load broken", search "save load": no rows.
findings.fix: Normalise both sides by removing punctuation and whitespace together, text.toLowerCase().replace(/[\p{P}\s]/gu, ""), so login, log-in, log in and save/load, save load all match
